observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a single standard four-way wooden pallet (stringer/block type) on bare concrete ground, viewed from slightly different angles, likely the same unit.
Photo 1 shows a visible crack/split in one of the top deck boards and visible nail heads.

Photo 2 shows large stacks of similar wooden pallets in what appears to be a warehouse yard with branded signage partly visible in the background; this looks like a stock/location photo rather than a close shot of the specific lot being sold.
No scale, weighing device, or weighing scene is shown in any photo.
No markings, stamps, or brand/grade stencils (e.g. EPAL, ISPM-15 heat-treat marks) are legible on the pallet surfaces.

claims.claim: Everything is clean, dry and sorted, no water added
claims.evidence: No way to assess moisture content or cleanliness from a static photo; wood could be damp or treated to add weight.

claims.claim: Weighed at 500 kg on a certified scale this morning
claims.evidence: No photo of a scale, weighbridge ticket, or the pallets being weighed is provided.

claims.claim: Standard wooden storage pallets (implying a batch/lot)
claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show only one pallet; photo 2 shows a large stack at what looks like a different, generic location, not confirmed to be the same lot for sale.

risks.risk: Quantity mismatch: unclear whether the sale is for a single pallet, a small number, or the full 500 kg lot implied by the weight claim.
risks.proof: A single photo showing the actual lot being sold, laid out and counted, ideally next to the scale reading.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a single pallet only, the one unit clearly shown in photos 0 and 1

risks.risk: Structural damage from the visible split board, which could mean the pallet is not fit for load-bearing reuse and only fit for scrap/firewood grade.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the split board and an underside shot showing the stringer/block condition.
risks.if_unproven: priced as damaged/scrap-grade wood, not intact reusable pallet

risks.risk: Weight padding via moisture (wetting wood increases weight, which matters if sold by weight).
risks.proof: A photo of a moisture meter reading on the wood, or a weighbridge ticket with date/time stamp.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if weight claim is unverified and lot is assumed drier/lighter than stated

risks.risk: Protruding or rusted nails posing handling/safety issues, common in used pallets.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the nail heads and board joints across several boards.
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing nail repair/rework before reuse

risks.risk: Photo 2 may be a stock/location photo not representing the actual pallets for sale, inflating perceived quantity or quality.
risks.proof: A fresh photo of the actual lot on the seller's current premises with a recognizable local landmark or timestamp.
risks.if_unproven: only the single pallet in photos 0 and 1 is treated as the confirmed item for sale

proof_requests: Photo or video of the actual weighing on the certified scale, showing the reading and the pallets being weighed.
Count and photo of all pallets included in this specific sale (not a generic warehouse stack).
Close-up of the split board and the underside/block structure of the pallet.
Confirmation of unit of sale: per pallet or per kg lot.
response.reason: The photos clearly show a standard wooden pallet with a visible defect, but the seller's wording implies a 500 kg bulk lot while only one pallet is clearly pictured, so the basic unit of sale (one pallet vs a weighed lot) cannot be determined, making even a worst-case price impossible without clarification.
